Interface RouteFilterSpec<S extends RouteFilterSpec<S>>

Type Parameters:
S - The type that declares the filters
All Known Subinterfaces:
HttpBodyRouteSpec<B>, HttpRouteGroup, HttpRouteSpec, RouteSpec<S>, ServerFilterSpec
public sealed interface RouteFilterSpec<S extends RouteFilterSpec<S>> permits RouteSpec<S>, ServerFilterSpec (not exhaustive)
Filter methods of handler routes: the filters of one route, see HttpRouteSpec, of every route of a group, see HttpRouteGroup, and of a server filter, see ServerFilterSpec. What declares a filter decides which requests it filters and when it runs among the other filters: the filter of a route filters the requests of that route, the filter of a group those of every route declared in the group, both after the server filters, and a server filter the requests its patterns match, ordered with the filter beans.

Request filters run in the order they are declared, and so do response filters, after the route. A response filter also filters a response a request filter answered with instead of the route, e.g. to add headers to a rejected request, when the response filter was declared on the same route or group as the request filter or on an enclosing group.

The request and the response filters come in the same four families, so that their lambdas are never ambiguous: before and after filters return nothing and change the request or the response in place, like a filter method with a MutableHttpRequest or MutableHttpResponse parameter that returns nothing; beforeReplacing and afterReplacing filters can also replace it, like a filter method returning a request or a response: a request filter answers the request instead of the route with the response it returns, or continues with the request it returns, e.g. with another method or body, see ReplacingRouteRequestFilter. Each has an asynchronous variant, and variants that change the propagated context.

Every filter method returns the FilterSpec of the filter it added: a filter runs on the thread of the filter chain, or on an executor chosen with ExecutionSpec.executeOn(String), like a filter method annotated @ExecuteOn, and FilterSpec.and() goes back to the route or the group to continue its declaration.

routes.GET("/orders/{id}")
    .before(request -> tenants.check(request)).executeOn(TaskExecutors.BLOCKING)
    .and()
    .after((request, response) -> response.header("X-Tenant", tenantOf(request))).and()
    .handle(orderHandler);

Matched routes only. As with the filter methods of a controller, the filters of a route and of its groups are route filters: they run only when that route matched the request. A request under the prefix of a group that no route answers (404), or that a route of the group would answer with another method or media type (405, 415, 406), does not run them. The filters of a server filter, declared with routes.filter(patterns...), pre-matching or not, and the @ServerFilter beans filter every request their patterns match, those responses included.

Like a filter method, a filter runs with the propagated context of the filter chain in scope, e.g. the MDC context an application filter added; to change it, see the variants that receive a MutablePropagatedContext.

  • Method Details

    • before

      FilterSpec<S> before(RouteRequestFilter filter)
      Filter the requests, like a @RequestFilter method that returns nothing. The filters of a route and of its groups run after the server filters, closest to the route: the filters of the outer group first, then those of the inner groups, then those of the route, each in the order they are declared. The filter of a route or a group runs only when the route, or a route of the group, matched the request: not for a 404 or a 405 under the prefix of the group, which only the server filters, pre-matching ones included, see.
      Parameters:
      filter - The filter, which can change the request in place
      Returns:
      The filter, to choose where it runs and to go back to the route or the group, see FilterSpec
      See Also:
      • RouteRequestFilter

      Parameters:

      Returns:
      The filter, to choose where it runs and to go back to the route or the group, see FilterSpec
      See Also:

    • before

      FilterSpec<S> before(ContextRouteRequestFilter filter)
      Filter the requests with a filter that changes the propagated context, like a @RequestFilter method with a MutablePropagatedContext parameter: what it adds is in scope for the next filters, the handler, the error routes and the response filters. Otherwise the same as before(RouteRequestFilter).
      Parameters:
      filter - The filter, which can change the request and the propagated context in place
      Returns:
      The filter, to choose where it runs and to go back to the route or the group, see FilterSpec
      See Also:
      • ContextRouteRequestFilter

    • beforeReplacing

      FilterSpec<S> beforeReplacing(ReplacingRouteRequestFilter filter)
      Filter the requests with a filter that can answer the request or replace it, like a @RequestFilter method returning a response or a request: a response it returns answers the request instead of the route, a request it returns is the request the filters after it and the route see, and null proceeds with the request it was given. Otherwise the same as before(RouteRequestFilter), which takes a filter that returns nothing, so that its lambdas are never ambiguous.
      Parameters:
      filter - The filter, which can answer the request instead of the route, or change or replace the request
      Returns:
      The filter, to choose where it runs and to go back to the route or the group, see FilterSpec
      See Also:
      • ReplacingRouteRequestFilter

    • after

      FilterSpec<S> after(RouteResponseFilter filter)
      Filter the responses, like a @ResponseFilter method. The response filters of a route and of its groups run after the route and before the response filters of the server filters: the filters of the route first, then those of the inner groups, then those of the outer group, each in the order they are declared. The filter of a route or a group runs only when the route, or a route of the group, matched the request: not for a 404 or a 405 under the prefix of the group, which only the server filters, pre-matching ones included, see.
      Parameters:
      filter - The filter
      Returns:
      The filter, to choose where it runs and to go back to the route or the group, see FilterSpec
